validation: Latest full lib272 green includes runtime::provider_eviction_tests; shared11-case bus compatibility runner previously green and unchanged. These records concern provider ownership/eviction assertions only; no broad RPC/runtime certification.

services/hub/internal/bus/register_hijac.note: Shared real embedded/WebSocket bus corpus proves first-live-provider ownership, idempotent self-registration, local-handler precedence, forged-response rejection and slot reclamation after disconnect. Actual Handle provider-eviction unit proves synchronous release/socket closure, immediate successor registration, unknown/builtin no-op and generation-fenced stale-probe refusal. Rust evicts by expected method owner rather than exposing an unfenced raw connection eviction: a stale probe cannot close a replacement or a builtin handler. A live unresponsive provider keeps its slot until that explicit liveness decision, preserving first-owner semantics.
